bull.last: RIVN: argues long. RIVN is deeply oversold (RSI 19.7) and trading 48.8% below its 52‑week high, placing it in a classic mean‑reversion zone. The stock has delivered strong EPS surprises for four consecutive quarters (+28.5% to +9.4%), and upcoming earnings on 2026‑10‑29 are expected to beat consensus, which could spark a bounce. Positive catalysts – a strategic NXP microcontroller partnership, early R1T reviews and the acquisition of an AI‑simulation firm – add credibility to its long‑term growth narrative. Analyst consensus is heavily bullish (20 buys vs 5 sells) with a mean price target of $19, implying ~63% upside from the current $11.63 level. Finally, the options market shows a bullish skew (put‑call ratio 0.2) and an implied 10.2% move, supporting short‑term upside.

bear.last: RIVN: RIVN is trading at $11.63, well below its 20‑day SMA ($13.44) and 200‑day SMA ($15.60), confirming a steep downtrend that makes any bounce fragile. The stock’s RSI of 19.7 signals extreme oversold conditions, but the low 20‑day volume ratio (0.49) and weak ATR‑based volatility (4.5%) suggest there is little buying pressure to sustain a move higher. Short interest sits at 14.9% of float with a short‑volume spike of 45.2% and only eight days to cover, meaning a short‑squeeze is possible but also that many traders are already betting on further declines. Upcoming earnings on 2026‑10‑29 carry an expected EPS of –$0.6366; while past quarters have posted positive surprises, the company’s net margin of –54.95% and negative ROE (–67.56%) indicate structural profitability problems that could outweigh any earnings beat. Finally, insider activity shows $788k of sales in the last 90 days and no hedge‑fund holdings, hinting that informed participants lack confidence in a sustained rally.

pm.last: RIVN: PASS. Despite being deeply oversold with an RSI under 20, RIVN is in a persistent structural downtrend below all major moving averages, and our desk rules and poor historical win rate on mean-reversion stock trades counsel against buying falling knives ahead of upcoming earnings.
